title: WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL -> SSSS (one global layer instead of three)
description: One string: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS", so layers 0-8 attend 1024 and only the forced last layer keeps the full 2048 context (was layers 3, 7, 9 global). short_window stays long//2; nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.986958 vs the 0.987227 baseline: -0.00027, a TIE (0.3 sigma on the round-3 arm-to-arm sd of 7.8e-4). 1124 steps, 294.6M tokens, MFU 40.59%, 34.6GB, FLOPs/token 4.13e8 (-3.5%). Train loss confirms the tie and is the lower-variance metric: mean over the last 60 logged steps is 2.7622 against a0's matched control 2.7625 -- indistinguishable. I ran this as the pre-registered defection from a 3-way collision on short_window//4 (a2, a3, me), moving the other coordinate of the window axis: they shrink what local layers see, I cut how many layers see globally. Two findings. (1) Cutting two of the three global layers costs nothing measurable, so a3's r03 all-L regression (+0.0025) was not 'less context is better' -- going the other way does not pay. The window axis is flat on the short side and only penalised on the long side, i.e. SSSL/SSSS is already at or past the plateau and the axis should be closed. (2) The FLOP saving did NOT convert into tokens: -3.5% FLOPs bought +0.24% tokens (294.6M vs 293.9M) and MFU fell 42.03 -> 40.59%. Combined with a3's finding that +12.8% FLOPs cost only 2.0% of tokens, the conclusion is that attention FLOPs are nearly free in BOTH directions here -- this box is overhead-bound, not FLOP-bound, so 'save FLOPs to buy tokens' is a dead strategy and only genuinely larger fwd/bwd shapes (a0/a1's device-batch-128) can move throughput.
